key_insight: TI-SAE turns a frozen clinical time-series model’s internal representations into reusable concepts describing when patterns occur and which variables are involved.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help researchers inspect patterns behind EHR-based predictions, but the abstract does not establish clinical utility or improved patient outcomes.
method: Learn a backbone-specific concept dictionary shared across patients from frozen model representations.
Define concepts using temporal Gaussian islands and sparse variable-composition vectors.
Use a separate selector to identify concepts driving each patient’s prediction.
evidence_signal: Evaluated across five backbone architectures on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, with three prediction tasks per dataset, TI-SAE reports strong faithfulness benchmark performance without numerical results in the abstract.
watch_item: Faithfulness to a model does not establish that learned concepts are clinically valid or generalize to other care settings.
paper_title: Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Clinical Time-Series Models
